title_en: Natanz nuclear site damaged: satellite images
text_en: Natanz nuclear site damaged: satellite images. The nuclear program of the ayatollahs is also behind Israel's attack against Iran. The IAEA report leaves little room for interpretation: Tehran has violated its commitments on the file. The agency has in fact denounced "numerous failures" in providing complete answers about its nuclear activities. A threat to the Jewish state, considering that the Islamic Republic has enough uranium enriched to 60 percent purity to build nine atomic bombs. In the first three days of the offensive, the damage count is considerable and is well summarized by satellite images of the Natanz site. The documents published by Maxar speak clearly: the Natanz facility has been heavily damaged by Israel's offensive. This is the beating heart of the Islamic Republic's nuclear program: located in the province of Isfahan, on a plain adjacent to the mountains south of Qom, it includes a fuel enrichment plant and a pilot fuel enrichment plant. Natanz consists of three underground buildings, two of which were designed to hold up to 50,000 centrifuges for uranium enrichment, and six above-ground buildings. Here Tehran has produced the vast majority of its nuclear fuel. And precisely for this reason Tel Aviv decided to put it at the top of its targets. Despite the propaganda of the ayatollahs - according to the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran, Natanz would have suffered only "superficial" damage - the satellite images show the extent of the Israeli offensive. Some signs had already been recorded in the previous days: videos of a fire circulated online, while the director of the IAEA confirmed that "the surface part of the pilot fuel enrichment plant has been destroyed". Israeli sources specified that, in addition to the surface damage, the underground was also hit, where various pieces of equipment are housed. Israel also targeted other facilities. There is no confirmation regarding the Fordow site - a more difficult target because it was built deep beneath a mountain - but offensives against the Tabriz and Arak facilities are reported. We recall that over the past three years Iran has raised uranium enrichment to 60 percent, reaching a step away from the 90 percent threshold that would allow the construction of nuclear weapons.

title_en: Induced earthquakes: can we cause earthquakes?
text_en: Induced earthquakes: can we cause earthquakes? Although earthquakes are usually associated with natural causes, the possibility that human activity can trigger them is not mere speculation. In recent years, industrial development has put the spotlight on the relationship between activities such as fracking, mining and the construction of large dams and the occurrence of induced earthquakes. International research agrees in attributing hundreds of tremors to these practices, although most have been of moderate magnitude. Fracking, a technique used to extract gas and oil from unconventional reservoirs, has been associated with an increase in seismicity in regions previously considered stable. According to the United States Geological Survey (USGS), the rate of earthquakes of magnitude greater than 3 in some producing areas multiplied tenfold during the last decade. The causality lies not so much in the fracturing itself, but in the injection of large volumes of wastewater at great depth. These changes in pore pressure and stress on pre-existing faults act as triggers for earthquakes. A study published in Science estimated that, in the south-central United States alone, induced seismicity came to account for 50% of all earthquakes recorded between 2013 and 2016. "If there is a nearby and vulnerable fault, changing the pressure may be enough to release it even with small human interventions," conclude the authors. In the case of mining, induced seismicity is generally of smaller magnitude, although it can affect surrounding areas and surface structures. Deep excavations, blasting and the emptying of large underground volumes alter geological stresses and, on occasion, have preceded microearthquakes. Research carried out in mines in South Africa, for example, revealed that 90% of the earthquakes in the Witwatersrand area were directly related to mining activity. The International Energy Agency notes that, although these earthquakes are usually felt only in the area of the mine, their monitoring is essential for the safety of workers and infrastructure. Large dams have produced some of the clearest examples of induced earthquakes. The phenomenon, known as "reservoir-induced seismicity", became notorious after the construction of the Koyna dam in India, linked to a magnitude 6.3 earthquake shortly after the reservoir was filled. Studies from that country's Institute of Geophysics indicate that the weight of millions of cubic meters of water on pre-existing faults can alter the tectonic balance of the region. According to data from the International Commission on Large Dams, some 100 dams worldwide have shown anomalous seismic activity linked to their reservoirs. Although these events tend to be more moderate than large tectonic earthquakes, they represent a risk to be considered in the design of new infrastructure. Specialists warn that not all human activities have the same potential to induce earthquakes. It depends mainly on local geological characteristics, the proximity of active faults and the volume of material injected or removed. For this reason, science promotes more

title_en: Miami Archdiocese criticizes $11 million cut to Catholic Charities for migrant minors
text_en: Miami Archdiocese criticizes $11 million cut to Catholic Charities for migrant minors. Miami Archdiocese criticizes the cancellation of a multimillion-dollar contract with Catholic Charities, which puts at risk the care of unaccompanied migrant minors. The Miami Archdiocese reacted to the announcement by the government of President Donald Trump of the cancellation of an $11 million contract with Catholic Charities in Miami, intended for the care of unaccompanied migrant minors. It stressed that the decision puts at risk a program with more than 60 years of operation focused on providing care to children who arrive alone in the country, a situation that the local Church considers worrying because of its immediate impact. Warning about the future of the program. Miami's archbishop, Thomas Wenski, expressed concern over the suspension of funding and warned that, without those resources, the program could run out of funds in approximately three months. Wenski said the contract was part of a historic collaboration between the Church and the federal government to care for unaccompanied migrant minors. "Those funds are for the contract we have had with the government for more than 60 years," the archbishop explained. "It was a way of collaborating with the government to provide treatment or protection for children who came to this country without being accompanied by their parents," he specified. Questions over the lack of explanations. The Archdiocese also questioned the lack of official information about the decision. Wenski said no clear reasons have been given for the suspension of funding. "It was unfortunately suspended, we don't know why," he said. The religious leader asked the federal government to reconsider the measure, considering that it directly affects the continuity of care for a vulnerable population. "We want the Federal Government to reconsider its decision," he added. Impact on a program considered a model. Catholic Charities' services in Miami have been recognized beyond the state as a model of care for unaccompanied migrant minors. The organization's chief executive, Peter Routsis Arroyo, noted that the program has even served as a reference for other institutions. According to him, the federal government itself has requested support to train other agencies and open similar centers. Background to the federal decision. The cancelled contract, valued at $11 million, was part of a relationship of more than six decades between Catholic Charities and the US government. According to information from the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), the decision responds to a reduction in the number of unaccompanied minors in the organization's care compared with previous administrations. HHS also noted that the Office of Refugee Resettlement is closing and consolidating facilities as part of federal efforts to control migration and the trafficking of minors. Possible short-term impact. The Archdiocese warned that, without the funding, the program could stop operating within three months, which would create uncertainty about the future of the minors who currently depend on these care services. title_en: West Sumatra Police Raid PETI in West Pasaman, Eight People Arrested
text_en: West Sumatra Police Raid PETI in West Pasaman, Eight People Arrested. TEMPO.CO, Jakarta - The West Sumatra Regional Police uncovered illegal gold mining activity (pertambangan emas tanpa izin, PETI) in West Pasaman Regency. The operation was carried out at two points on the Batang Batahan River, Jorong Silaping, Kenagarian Batahan, Sungai Beremas District, early on Wednesday, 12 February 2025. The Head of the Public Relations Division of West Sumatra Police, Senior Commissioner Dwi Sulistyawan, said this action was part of the police's efforts to crack down on illegal mines that have the potential to damage the environment and cause social and economic impacts on the surrounding community. He continued that during the operation, the Subdirectorate 4 Special Crimes Team of the Special Criminal Directorate of West Sumatra Police secured eight people suspected of being involved in the illegal gold mining activity. "We have secured several perpetrators along with the equipment used in the mining. This illegal activity not only violates the law, but also has a bad impact on the environment, including river pollution and forest destruction," said Dwi in his official statement on Friday, 14 February 2025. From the scene, officers seized two heavy equipment units, a Kobelco SK 200 XD in blue and a SANY SY 215 in yellow, five wooden dulang (gold pans), and five sheets of carpet used in the mining process. The perpetrators are currently undergoing examination to uncover a wider network. Their identities are AS (25), a resident of Jorong Silaping who acted as field supervisor; H (52), a North Sumatra resident as operator of the Kobelco heavy equipment; and JLH (32), a Simalungun, North Sumatra resident, who also acted as operator of the Kobelco heavy equipment. Next, RU (23), a West Pasaman resident who acted as field supervisor; J (49), a West Pasaman resident as a Box worker; DL (31), a Mandailing Natal resident as a Box worker; AM (19), a Mandailing Natal resident as a Box worker; and ID (41), a Riau resident who acted as operator of the SANY SY 215 heavy equipment. As of now, eight perpetrators remain detained at West Sumatra Police, while the evidence has been placed at the West Pasaman Resort Police. The investigation continues to thoroughly probe the case and prevent further losses for the community and environment. Dwi stated that West Sumatra Police will continue to conduct operations and patrols in areas prone to PETI to prevent similar illegal activities. The public is also urged not to get involved in illegal mining practices, given the legal risks and the environmental impact they cause. "We will firmly act against anyone involved in illegal mining activity. We also invite the public to play an active role in reporting suspicious activities so that the environment is preserved and the law can be enforced," he said. title_en: Formula 1: what Jack Doohan said about the crash that left him out of the Australian GP
text_en: Formula 1: what Jack Doohan said about the crash that left him out of the Australian GP. The great spectacle of Formula 1 raised the curtain for the first time this season, in Australia. But, due to bad weather conditions, it had some eventful moments. The Australian Jack Doohan (Alpine), so much in everyone's mouth because of the pressure exerted by Franco Colapinto as the team's reserve driver, was one of those affected: he slid on the wet track, hit his car against a wall, and had to retire from the race before completing the first lap.

title_en: With Lospennato and the Macris, PRO closed its campaign: it asked porteños for their vote and harshly criticized Larreta and Bullrich
text_en: With Lospennato and the Macris, PRO closed its campaign: it asked porteños for their vote and there were harsh criticisms of Larreta and Bullrich. In line with a campaign of unprecedented high voltage for what is only a legislative election in the city of Buenos Aires, PRO closed with an event in Villa Pueyrredón before 2,500 people. Silvia Lospennato was the main speaker as the lead candidate on the list, but cousins Jorge and Mauricio Macri launched very harsh criticisms of former party leaders and also of the Government. At an event that lasted a little over an hour at the 17 de Agosto club in Villa Pueyrredón, the speakers were Lospennato, the Macris, María Eugenia Vidal and Fernán Quirós. The basketball gym was packed with 2,500 people who surrounded the leaders, who spoke from a platform located at midcourt. Macrismo appeared optimistic ahead of the election, and sources from Uspallata privately expressed confidence in a very competitive performance, even though most polls show Lospennato in third place behind the Peronist candidate Leandro Santoro and the government's Manuel Adorni. The presidential spokesperson was practically not mentioned at the event. The main barbs were aimed at Santoro as the representative of Kirchnerism, but especially at former PRO figures such as Horacio Rodríguez Larreta and Patricia Bullrich. The one who hit hardest at those who were presidential pre-candidates in 2023 was Mauricio Macri, their former political leader. "PRO is united, PRO is standing again. I can say positively, and we have publicly self-criticized, that the internal contest of '23 was very damaging to our space, and that the two candidates let themselves be corrupted by ego and excessive ambition, but the two of them are no longer here, they have left", he said. And he taunted them when their names came up: "Out, out, out, bad energy, bad vibes." The crowd applauded him and shouted "Mauricio president." The barbs at Larreta did not stop there. Jorge Macri took up the baton at the right moment, before Lospennato's speech, and was very clear about his challenge to the man who was head of government from 2015 to 2023 and has now launched his own list. "In these elections, legislators are being elected. These candidates who present themselves saying they want to be head of government seem strange. Basically they are saying 'give me two more years while I prepare to compete in the next one'," Macri said to him. And then he urged him on. "You know what? If you want to be a legislator, go and be a legislator, brother. The head of government post is in two years, and I'll be waiting for you there," said the current mayor, applauded by those present at the same club where four months ago he asked for his cousin's candidacy in the October national elections. The Macri cousins had a situation that caused some tension, although it was later played down. "Are you making eyes at me?" In a world that is becoming increasingly digital, cryptocurrency as digital currency is today becoming very popular among the younger generation. Most people have a desire to make high profits in a short time. Those who issue cryptocurrencies use this to make profits. Although the value of cryptocurrencies runs into lakhs, small investors are also keen to invest, since even Rs. 100 can be invested in them. But do people make profits by investing, or do they lose money? What exactly is happening in the crypto market? Many people have this question. But none of these are questions that can be answered easily, because of the nature of its technology. What is cryptocurrency? Cryptocurrency means digital currencies. Cryptocurrencies cannot be counterfeited. Cryptocurrencies are created using blockchain network technology. No government intervention can be made in cryptocurrencies. Cryptocurrencies have no borders either. In short, they are not under anyone's control. The details of who is doing it and how they are doing it are also not known to the outside. Each cryptocurrency has a specific value. The value of each coin rises and falls according to the market. Goods or services can also be bought using cryptocurrencies. Cryptocurrencies are decentralized. That is, no company controls crypto coins. Is it only Bitcoin? Many people think that only Bitcoin is cryptocurrency. In fact there are hundreds of coins. After Bitcoin, which was created first, the Ethereum coin became popular. For a long time these two were in competition. Now various cryptocurrencies such as Dogecoin have arrived. Fraud? Illicit money can also be invested in cryptocurrencies. It is said that this is used as one of the ways to bring black money into circulation. Since illegal and unlawful transactions cannot be carried out through bank transactions, they are carrying them out through such means. Because of this too, governments want to ban it. India strongly opposes it. India also strongly opposes cryptocurrencies. The reason is that if the dominance of digital currency increases, the value of the country's currency and the need for currency itself will be questioned. This hesitation exists not only in India but in many countries of the world. To regulate cryptocurrency, a bill is being prepared in India under the name of the Official Digital Currency Regulation Bill 2021. What will the future be? Price rises and falls in cryptocurrencies happen very quickly. An investor must be as ready to lose money as they are eager to earn money as quickly as possible. Moreover, getting back the invested money safely also remains questionable. Because of this, cryptocurrency remains an unsolved puzzle. > This is part of a premium article by Nellai Jena published in Hindu Tamil Thisai. New Delhi: The central government has given a clarification in Parliament on LIC's investment in Adani Group shares. The government told Parliament that the insurance company LIC (Life Insurance Corporation) has said that it strictly follows all rules when making investments. After the share prices of Adani group companies fell in the stock market, LIC's investment in Adani Group companies has raised questions, and political attacks have also been made against the government. In a written reply to a question asked by BJP MP Sushil Kumar Modi in the Rajya Sabha, Finance Minister Bhagwat Karad said that LIC has informed the government that all its investments were made in accordance with the Insurance Act, 1938 and the IRDA Investment Regulations, 2016. They are carried out with strict compliance and are guided by the company's operating system. He said that KHOU [unclear token, likely LIC] has also clarified that most information related to its investments is available to the public. On 30 January 2023, LIC issued a statement clarifying its investments in Adani Group companies. LIC said that in the past few years it has bought shares worth 30,129 crore rupees in Adani Group companies, whose market value, based on the closing price of "56 January 2023" [as printed in the source], is 56,142 crore rupees. According to LIC, up to 31 December 2022 the total value of its investment in Adani Group companies was 35,917.31 crore rupees, and up to today LIC's total investment in the Adani group is 36,474.78 crore rupees. On the other hand, LIC said that the Adani Group accounts for only 0.975 per cent of its total assets under management at book value, whereas the total assets under LIC's management are 41.66 lakh crore rupees.

Liputan6.com, Jakarta - Registration for Government Employees with Work Agreements (PPPK) officially opened this Tuesday (12/2/2019). Online PPPK registration is open for the next 5 days. This follows the steps of the Ministry of State Apparatus Empowerment and Bureaucratic Reform (PANRB), which officially issued PANRB Ministerial Regulation (Permen) Number 2 of 2019 governing the procurement of PPPK. "Online PPPK registration will start today, Tuesday, 12 February 2019, and will close on 17 February 2019," said the Head of the Legal, Communication and Public Information Bureau of the PANRB Ministry, Mudzakir, in Jakarta. According to Mudzakir, the PANRB Regulation stipulates that online registration is carried out through the website sscasn.bkn.go.id. PPPK selection at this stage is open to former K-II honorary staff who took the test in 2013 for teaching, lecturing and health worker positions listed in the database of the National Civil Service Agency (BKN). Specifically for Agricultural Extension Workers (Penyuluh Pertanian), the database is held by BKN and the Ministry of Agriculture. The competency selection for PPPK will cover managerial competence, technical competence and sociocultural competence, carried out using a Computer Assisted Test (CAT) system. The PPPK selection will also include a computer-based interview to assess integrity and morality. For teaching positions, the minimum qualification required is an S-1 (Strata Satu) or D-4 (Diploma Four) degree, and the candidate must still be actively teaching. Meanwhile, for lecturer positions, the minimum qualification required is an S-2 (Strata Dua) degree and the candidate must still be actively serving in a government institution.
